symptom: The exported request transcript digest accepted a TypeScript-typed but runtime caller-controlled request and directly read nested fields while hashing. A Proxy could return a later repaired value through get while its own-data descriptor still represented a malformed initial freeze timestamp or correction content digest. The hash could therefore describe a later claim rather than the entry-time metadata; it never established independent authority.
lesson: An exported digest helper is an independent runtime input boundary: its static request type does not guarantee the caller passed an immutable preflight-built request. Hashing direct nested reads can accept a repaired claim even when a descriptor-only snapshot would reject its original malformed fields.
guardrail: Before standalone transcript hashing, detach the entire bounded own-data-descriptor request graph and check exact structural fields and scalar types. Hash only the detached copy; assert adversarial freeze and correction-revision descriptor traps fire, getters never execute, and valid synthetic request digests remain stable. Never treat a digest as evidence authentication or scoring authority.
